lnp0.title: LockedNet
lnp0.t1: LockedNet was an ambitious attempt to develop a decentralized anti-blackout ecosystem capable of maintaining essential household functions independently of external power and communication infrastructure. The project involved system architecture design, low-power wireless communication concepts, embedded device planning, and local software development.
lnp0.t2: However, as development progressed, it became clear that the project's scope significantly exceeded the available resources and my experience at the time. The lack of a sufficiently defined MVP also led to repeated architectural revisions and shifting priorities. Rather than continuing development without a clear path toward a validated solution, I decided to discontinue the project and focus on smaller, more achievable engineering challenges.
lnp0.t3: Although LockedNet never reached the stage of a fully integrated and tested system, it provided valuable experience in system design, technical feasibility assessment, and project scope management.
lnp0.t4: The original documentation remains available as an archive of the development process. It includes conceptual designs and experimental implementations that should not be interpreted as a validated, production-ready system.
